newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian General News - Feb 20.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

According to industry sources, the United States Undersecretary of State for global affairs, Tim Wirth, told a recent business briefing on United Nations climate change talks that the US would consider imposing trade sanctions on Australia if the Federal overnment keeps its promise not to sign any convention on climate change and greenhouse gas emissions. Page 1.

The A$1.1 billion Century Zinc case will now certainly go to formal arbitration before the Native Title Tribunal after hopes of a negotiated solution to the native title impasse surrounding the project were dashed yesterday with the collapse of last-ditchtalks in Mount Isa. Page 1.

Under a proposal coordinated by the Australian Chamber of Commerce and Industry, employer groups have moved to fast-track the stripping back of industrial awards covering almost 100,000 workers in the retail, hospitality, health and printing industries. The groups have applied to the Australian Industrial Relations Commission to have six large Federal awards pared back to the 20 basic award entitlements allowed under the new Workplace Relations Act. Page 3.

Arnotts' move to withdraw biscuits in Australia because of an extortion threat, combined with a Taiwanese newspaper report that quarantine officials here had stepped up inspection of the company's products, has led major supermarkets in Taiwan to strip Arotts' products from their shelves. Page 5.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The Howard Government became embroiled in a controversy over appointments to statutory bodies yesterday after Cabinet blocked an attempt by Health Minister Michael Wooldridge to appoint Professor John Funder, a doctor who supports the abortion pill, as th head of the National Health and Research Council, and an attempt by Primary Industries Minister John Anderson to appoint former labor treasurer John Kerin as the chairman of the Australian Meat and Livestock Corporation. Page 1.

After meeting with Papua New Guinean Prime Minister Sir Julius Chan in Port Moresby, Foreign Affairs Minister Alexander Downer announced yesterday Australia would be supporting Papua New Guinea's progress towards Bougainville peace by freeing up a A$4 milion emergency and medical relief package. Page 1.

In an interview with The Australian yesterday, Industry Minister John Moore dashed car industry hopes for a special exemption by describing free trade for Australia by 2010 as "inevitable". Moore pledged Government support to aid industry's adjustment to ree and open trade by that deadline. Page 1.

According to a report prepared by the National Health and Medical Research Council, expected to be considered by the Australian Health Ministers' Advisory Council today, hospitals are re-using disposable devices in breach of guidelines by State and Territry Governments and manufacturers. Page 3.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

In an interview with the Herald yesterday, Prime Minister John Howard blocked the State push for radical reforms to rein in the High Court's powers by ruling out any change to the system of appointing High Court judges. Howard said he understood State conerns about the court's judicial activism, but said he would not countenance any change to the existing system. Page 1.

Following the ABC's decision to broadcast the ACTU-sponsored Whitlam lecture 10 days ago, the corporation's chairman, Donald McDonald, has contacted several board members to discuss the seriousness of the lapse of judgement by management. Many believe ABC managing director Brian Johns may be vulnerable to an inquiry by his own board over the decision. Page 1.

Leading medical and scientific figures, including Australian Medical Association president Keith Wollar, were angered last night at Federal Cabinet's decision to reject the appointment of Professor John Funder as chair of the National Health and Medical Rsearch Council - Australia's most prestigious medical research body - after pressure from Independent Senator Brian Harradine. Page 1.

Alleged Australian paedophile Philip Bell has 15 days under the South African Extradition Act in which to file a Supreme Court appeal against magistrate Floris van Zyl's decision to have Bell extradited to Australia. Page 1.
THE AGE

Despite a concerted push by State Governments to adopt an American judicial model which would see the States gain control of the appointment and dismissal of High Court judges, Prime Minister John Howard emphatically rejected the proposal, saying it wouldturn the process into a circus. Page 1.

Speaking on The 7.30 Report last night, Victorian Police Minister Bill McGrath provoked an outcry by admitting he had "great reservations" about gay and lesbian officers in the State Police. The comments prompted the Civil Liberties Council to suggest McGath might have breached anti-discrimination laws, and a representative of gay police branded the comments homophobic. Page 1.

Two Brisbane-based lawyers with experience in international peace negotiations have won support from warring parties for a plan, which the Howard Government has secretly offered to fund, which would see expert international conflict negotiators helping toend Bougainville's nine-year war. Page 1.

In the most detailed picture of Victorian gamblers yet, figures compiled by the Addiction Research Institute have revealed the number of calls to the State's gambling crisis line, G-Line, has jumped by 183 per cent in the past year to almost 10,000. The fgures show poker machines are the biggest cause of gambling problems, affecting almost three quarters of all gamblers who called the service. Page 1.
-- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
